parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: A pupil tests the effect of water temperature on sugar dissolving time. Identify the independent and dependent variables and one control.
ms: Control sugar mass, water volume, stirring or particle size

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: A balance reads 3 g with nothing on it. Explain the type of error and how to improve the measurement.
ms: Tare/calibrate before use; averaging alone does not remove the offset

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: A microscope has a ×12 eyepiece and ×10 objective. Find total magnification and state one rule for a clear biological drawing.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: Explain how a plant leaf cell differs from an animal cell, giving three relevant structures.
ms: Large permanent vacuole; contrast with typical animal cell

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: Explain why a pair of antagonistic muscles is needed to bend and straighten a joint.
ms: The opposing muscle contracts for the reverse

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: Use the particle model to explain why a gas fills its container but a solid keeps its shape.
ms: Gas particles move randomly with large gaps
Solid particles vibrate around fixed positions

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Describe how to obtain salt crystals from a mixture of dry salt and sand.

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: A lamp takes in 240 J and transfers 36 J as useful visible light. Find its efficiency and unwanted transfer.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: A 1.5 kW heater runs for 2 hours at an assumed 24 p/kWh. Calculate energy and cost.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: Compare inherited and environmental variation, using one suitable example of each.
ms: Inherited differences arise from genetic information
Examples such as ABO blood group and a scar, accepting appropriate interaction explanations

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: Describe fertilisation and implantation in humans, including their usual locations.
ms: Embryo implants in uterine lining later

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: Explain two adaptations of an insect-pollinated flower.
ms: Nectar/sticky pollen with a correct link to pollen transfer

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: Explain how pollination differs from fertilisation in flowering plants.
ms: Pollination transfers pollen from anther to stigma
Pollen tube then grows towards an ovule
Fertilisation fuses male and egg nuclei

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: State three conditions commonly needed for seed germination, explaining one.
ms: Suitable temperature, with explanation such as oxygen for aerobic respiration

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: A pupil says a strong acid must be concentrated. Explain why this is incorrect.
ms: Concentration is amount per solution volume
A strong acid can be dilute

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: Name the products when zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid and describe a test for the gas.
ms: A small gas sample gives a squeaky pop with a lighted splint under supervision

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Given magnesium is more reactive than copper, predict what happens when magnesium is put in copper sulfate solution.
ms: Copper is produced because magnesium is more reactive

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: Two parallel branches carry 0.35 A and 0.45 A. Find supply current and explain the principle.
ms: Charge is conserved at the junction

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: A resistor has 9 V across it and carries 0.3 A. Find its resistance and describe the voltmeter connection.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: Explain why the total energy of a bouncing ball and its surroundings is conserved even though each rebound is lower.
ms: Energy transfers to thermal stores and sound in surroundings

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: In grass → grasshopper → bird, predict two possible effects of a fall in grasshopper numbers and give one limitation.
ms: Grass may be eaten less and increase
Birds may have less food and decline
Other food sources/interactions may alter the outcome

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: Describe how random quadrats can estimate a plant population in a field.
ms: Random coordinates and consistent quadrat area/counting
Calculate mean per unit area from sufficient samples
Multiply by field area, acknowledging sampling uncertainty

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: A trolley travels 3.6 m in 6 s. Find average speed and state one way to reduce timing error.
ms: Electronic timing or a longer measured interval with justification

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: Explain the forces on a parachutist falling at terminal velocity.
ms: Drag acts up with equal magnitude

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: Distinguish an element, a compound and a mixture using suitable examples.
ms: Element one atom type, e.g. iron
Compound chemically bonded elements in fixed ratio, e.g. water
Mixture substances together without chemical combination, e.g. air

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: State the reactivity trends down Group 1 and Group 7, and predict whether chlorine can displace bromine from a bromide solution.
ms: Chlorine displaces bromine because chlorine is more reactive

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Explain how alveoli are adapted for gas exchange.
ms: Blood supply and ventilation maintain concentration differences

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: Explain the roles of enzymes and villi in digestion and absorption.
ms: Enzymes break large molecules into small soluble products
Thin surface/blood supply supports transfer to circulation

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: Describe the positive iodine test and explain what a negative result does and does not show.
ms: Negative means starch was not detected under the test conditions
Other carbohydrates can still be present

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: Explain why nicotine vaping should not be described as harmless for young people.
ms: Developing lungs/brains can be sensitive to effects
Less harmful than smoking does not mean risk-free or appropriate for non-smokers

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: A wave has frequency 8 Hz and wavelength 0.5 m. Calculate speed and explain frequency.
ms: Frequency is complete oscillations per second

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: Explain how a higher-pitched sound differs from a louder sound.
ms: Louder sound relates to greater amplitude/intensity

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: A ray hits a plane mirror at 28° to the normal. Find reflection angle and angle to the mirror surface.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: A reaction in an open flask loses measured mass as gas escapes. Explain why this does not violate conservation of mass.
ms: Atoms/mass still exist outside the flask
A complete closed-system total is conserved

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: Explain exothermic reactions using energy needed to break bonds and energy released when bonds form.
ms: More is released than required overall, warming surroundings

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: Explain why a catalyst can produce more gas after 30 seconds but the same final gas total.
ms: Same limiting reactant amount can produce the same total

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: State the aerobic respiration word equation and distinguish respiration from breathing.
ms: Respiration is a cellular chemical process transferring energy
Breathing moves air in and out

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: State yeast fermentation products and explain one use in bread making.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: Explain why brighter light stops increasing pondweed oxygen production beyond a certain point.
ms: Another factor such as carbon dioxide becomes limiting
Increasing only light cannot remove the new limitation

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: A pupil claims warm dye spreads faster only because of diffusion. Suggest a control and explain an alternative process and a limitation.
ms: Same dye amount/vessel/volume and no stirring
Observed spreading alone cannot isolate molecular diffusion

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: Explain why a compass aligns near a bar magnet and state the field-line direction outside it.
ms: It experiences a turning effect in the field
Outside field lines run north to south

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: Describe an electromagnet relay and explain one benefit of a controllable magnet.
ms: Current in a coil produces a field
Field attracts an armature to operate a switch
Switching current can control/release the action

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: A 30 N force moves a load 2.5 m in its direction. Calculate work and explain the unit.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: A 15 N force at 0.4 m balances another force at 0.6 m. Find the other force.

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: Explain how a vacuum flask reduces conduction, convection and radiation.
ms: Vacuum prevents convection across the gap

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: Explain how burning fossil fuels changes the carbon cycle and can affect climate.
ms: Transfers stored carbon into atmospheric carbon dioxide
Changed energy balance contributes to warming

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Explain why aluminium is commonly extracted by electrolysis while some less reactive metal oxides can be reduced with carbon.
ms: Carbon can reduce oxides of metals below it
Aluminium is more reactive than carbon

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: Give two environmental benefits and one limitation of recycling metals.

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: Describe evolution by natural selection in three linked stages.
ms: Differential survival and reproduction under a selection pressure
Advantageous alleles become more common across generations

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: Explain why a conservation breeding programme alone may not save a wild species.
ms: Needs sufficient genetic diversity and successful breeding
Suitable habitat/threat reduction is also needed
Without these, released animals may not establish a viable population

parts.title: Question 1
parts.q: Explain the relationship between DNA, chromosomes and genes.
ms: Alleles are versions of a gene

parts.title: Question 2
parts.q: For a hypothetical single-gene trait, cross Aa with Aa. Give the genotype ratio and recessive phenotype probability.

parts.title: Question 3
parts.q: An ultrasound pulse returns after 0.00008 s in a medium with speed 1500 m/s. Find the reflector depth.

parts.title: Question 4
parts.q: Compare sound and electromagnetic waves in terms of medium and ionisation.
ms: Sound needs a medium, EM can cross vacuum
High-energy EM such as X-rays can ionise

parts.title: Question 5
parts.q: Describe how igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks form.
ms: Sedimentary from deposited material compacted/cemented or other valid sedimentary process

parts.title: Question 6
parts.q: Explain ordinary Moon phases and why they do not require an eclipse.
ms: Moon reflects sunlight with about half illuminated
We see different fractions of that half during orbit
Earth’s shadow causes lunar eclipses, not normal phases

parts.title: Question 7
parts.q: Explain Earth’s seasons using axial tilt rather than Earth–Sun distance.
ms: Hemisphere towards Sun has longer days
Higher sunlight angle increases energy received per area

parts.title: Question 8
parts.q: A spring extends 0.025 m under 5 N. Find its spring constant and give one limitation of the model.
ms: Proportional relation only below limit of proportionality

parts.title: Question 9
parts.q: A 480 N force acts over 0.024 m². Find pressure and explain the effect of doubling area at fixed force.

parts.title: Question 10
parts.q: Explain how a hydraulic system can increase output force without creating energy.
ms: Pressure change transmitted through enclosed fluid
Larger output area gives larger force
Larger output piston moves a shorter distance in the ideal system
